doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Always knowing he'd be a musician
summary: He always wanted to play trumpet like Harry James and loved all show business and audience acceptance.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What really sold you as far as being — at what point in your career as a youth did you say “I’m going to be a musician all my life.”

Oh always. I knew that before I got the trumpet. I wanted to play and that was to me — Harry James, to see him, I just loved Harry James and I wanted to be like that, and I wanted to play the trumpet, and I loved the trumpet. That was always what I wanted to do. So I always knew what I wanted to do. That was a great thing I guess, not wondering or anything. And I always loved all kinds of show business. I liked the playing and the singing and acting.
Yeah. So it wasn’t purely just the music. It was the whole spectrum.

The acceptance. Yeah, being in front of an audience and getting the reaction from the people, I guess getting that love, and wanting that love and wanting to play.
